name: Israel Katz
role: Israeli Defense Minister (2024-); Likud; earlier Foreign (2019-20, 2024), Finance, Transport and other minister
summary: Israel Katz is a Likud politician on the hawkish right. He holds that Israel is the Jewish people's nation-state in its historical homeland, rejects a Palestinian state and has pushed settlement expansion, and as Defense Minister has ordered strikes on Iran, held ground in Gaza and Syria, and sought a voluntary-emigration plan for Gazans. In earlier posts he favoured competition and private operators in transport, and as Defense Minister he proposed a gradual ultra-Orthodox draft.

civil-marriage.rationale: He voted in 2018 against bills to allow civil marriage.

conscription.rationale: He voted in 2013 against the bill to abolish compulsory conscription, and as Defense Minister pursued a draft of ultra-Orthodox men.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: He voted in 2023 to advance the bill removing the reasonableness standard from judicial review, limiting court review of government decisions.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: He initiated a 2000 bill giving a zero VAT rate to basic goods and services.

death-penalty.rationale: He voted for the 2026 Death Penalty for Terrorists Law at third reading.

direct-votes.rationale: He initiated a Basic Law on referendums and a bill to put the West Bank and Jordan Valley to a referendum, so major decisions would go to direct votes.

force-without-un.rationale: As Defense Minister he led Israel's June 2025 strike on Iran, which he called preemptive, without any UN Security Council approval.

free-public-college.rationale: He initiated a 1999 bill to extend free education to the end of the first degree.

historical-land-claim.rationale: In 2019 he said no one can separate the Jewish people from their historical homeland, rooting Israel's claim in thousands of years of Jewish history.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: He initiated a 2000 Basic Law bill defining Israel as the state of the Jewish people and voted for the 2018 Nation-State Law of the Jewish People.

legalize-drugs.rationale: He voted against the 2023 bill to regulate the cannabis market for personal use.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: As Transport Minister he said competition is more important than privatization and credited competition in rail, ports and aviation with cutting prices.

minority-language-support.rationale: He initiated the 2022 bill creating a national authority for Aramaic culture and language, and a parallel Judeo-Moroccan one.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: His ministry's decade of reforms included opening public transport to private operators and budgeting the privatization of Egged, the bus company.

national-self-determination.rationale: He answered French moves to recognise Palestine by saying Israel would build 'the Jewish Israeli state' in the West Bank, which denies a Palestinian state there.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: He initiated bills to cancel the Oslo, Hebron and Wye agreements, to apply Israeli sovereignty to Area C and to annex the Jordan Valley, the opposite of trading land for peace agreements.

recognise-genocide.rationale: He initiated the 2021 bill to recognise the Armenian genocide and mark a memorial day.

refugee-return.rationale: He initiated the 2001 law entrenching the negation of a right of return for refugees.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: He initiated a 2002 Law of Return amendment to recognise only conversion according to halacha, giving one interpretation legal precedence.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: He initiated bills on the purchase rights of public-housing tenants in 2000 and 2002.

territorial-expansion.rationale: In March 2025 he said Hamas would lose territory 'which will be annexed to Israel' and that Israel would take more of Gaza for permanent control; in 2025 he said the IDF would stay on Hermon and in Syria indefinitely.

notes:
Rules 7, new audit, second pass. Evidence: his 2019 UN General Assembly speech (primary words, UNGDC), his Knesset record from the local Knesset corpus (plenum votes 2003-2026, 12,386 of them, and 244 bills he initiated or joined; titles are Hebrew, given with an English gloss), his direct statements as quoted in full-text press articles (Jerusalem Post, Ynet, Times of Israel, JNS: March 2025 Gaza annexation statement, July 2025 Sweida joint statement, Syria buffer zone), a Globes interview, and two 2017 CNN transcripts (mediasum CNN-321522 and CNN-329430), which hold only a one-line remark on Iran in Syria and one on a Western Wall rail station and settle nothing. UNSC, EUSpeech, WEF and other UNGDC years hold nothing from him.
Record over words: where a Knesset vote or a bill he initiated settles a statement, it alone answers (jewish-state-israel, no-land-for-peace, refugee-return, death-penalty, conscription); a bill he only initiated is medium except where it states the position in its own title. Votes against opposition private bills are given weight only where the bill's subject is the statement (cannabis, civil marriage, abolishing conscription, reasonableness bill); coalition discipline could explain them, so they stay medium.
Searched by theme and left null where nothing settled: economy and labour (his votes on minimum wage, emergency worker protection, strikes and no-confidence motions fit either answer or are coalition-discipline votes), civil liberties (his votes against adding equality to the Basic Laws and the Nation-State Law in 2018, 2023 and 2025 fit either answer), religion and state (votes on Sabbath transport, conversion by city rabbis, the rabbinical courts law pull in different directions, and the 2017 Shabbat train compromise and 2010 compliance with the court on gender-segregated buses likewise), security and foreign policy beyond the cited acts (the ICC, the UN, UNRWA votes map to no statement), the judiciary beyond the 2023 reasonableness bill, women and gender, ecology (he voted for the 2021 Climate Law as a coalition bill, a single act that does not settle drastic-climate-action).
His October 2023 X post, as embedded in JNS ('no electrical switch will be turned on, no water hydrant opened, no fuel truck will enter until the Israeli abductees are returned home... Humanitarian for humanitarian'), was checked against civilians-legitimate-targets, torture-always-illegal and the war statements; it presents the siege as leverage for the hostages, not a claim that civilians are legitimate targets, so it settles none of them.
Press reports of his acts as Defense Minister are tier 3 (medium at most). Not reached: Hebrew-language interviews and X posts, gov.il texts, committee protocols, Knesset speeches.
